Dominic Greene''' (born February 21, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] for one year before being selected with the 28th overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.syracuse.com/today/index.ssf/2008/06/donte_goes_xxth_to.html |title=Donte Greene traded to Houston |work=Syracuse.com |date=June 26, 2008 |access-date=September 21, 2013}} ==Early life== Greene was born on the [[Munich-Riem Airport|United States Air Force Base in Munich, Germany]]. His mother worked for the [[National Security Agency]].{{cite web|last=Lidz|first=Franz|title=Greener Pastures|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1106915/index.htm|work=SI.com|access-date=July 28, 2012|date=January 22, 2007|archive-date=February 1, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100201200419/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1106915/index.htm|url-status=dead}} In the mid-1990s, Greene's parents divorced. Greene then attended school in [[Japan]] before returning to [[Germany]] and eventually [[Hanover, Pennsylvania]]. In October 2001, Greene's mother died of a [[heart attack]], and Greene moved to [[Woodlawn, Baltimore County, Maryland]] with his father and brother.{{cite web|last=McMullen|first=Paul|title=Greene, mom forever a team|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2007/01/17/greene-mom-forever-a-team/|work=BaltimoreSun.com|access-date=July 28, 2012|date=January 17, 2007}} Greene was named as a 2006 USA Men's U18 National Team member on June 26, 2006. He averaged 3.5 points and 1.0 rebounds per game as the USA captured a 4–0 mark and the gold medal at the 2006 FIBA Americas U18 Championship for Men in [[San Antonio, Texas]]. He was a 2007 [[McDonald's All-American]], Maryland's 2007 Gatorade Player of the Year, was named to the Nike Brand All-America Team and selected to play in the 2007 Jordan Classic.[http://www.usab.com/biosmen/donte_greene_bio.html Donte Greene Bio]{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In the class of 2007, he ranked as the No. 7 overall recruit and No. 2 power forward by Scout.com and as No. 10 overall and the No. 3 small forward by Rivals.com. Greene graduated in 2007 from [[Towson Catholic High School]], where he averaged 18.4 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 2.1 steals and 4.3 blocks per game as a senior in 2006–07, and helped Towson Catholic to a 32–6 record and to its second consecutive Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association A Conference and Baltimore Catholic League titles. Greene again played on Team USA in the 2007 USA Basketball U19 World Championships. Although he was slowed by a shoulder injury, Greene played in eight-of-nine contests and averaged 4.3 points and 1.5 rebounds. The team took home the silver medal after losing to [[Serbia]] in the championship game.{{cite web|url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4467|title=DONTE' GREENE – 2007 MEN'S BASKETBALL|work=suathletics.com|access-date=September 29, 2013}} ==College career== In his freshman year of college, Greene started all 35 games he appeared in and led Syracuse in scoring with 17.7 points to go along with 7.2 rebounds per game. He became the first Syracuse freshmen since [[Carmelo Anthony]] to lead Syracuse in scoring, while setting a new SU freshmen record for 3-pointers in one season, notching 90, surpassing [[Gerry McNamara]], who previously held the record with 85. Greene also led Syracuse with 57 blocks. He was named to the Big East All-Rookie Team.[http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2008/04/syracuse_freshman_donte_greene.html Syracuse freshman Donte Greene to enter NBA draft] Greene had 19 points and 13 rebounds in an 85–73 Syracuse victory over [[Seton Hall University|Seton Hall]] on March 5, 2008.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280652550 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720183523/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280652550 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 20, 2012 |title=Syracuse 85, Seton Hall 73 |work=ESPN.com |date=March 5, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2013}} Greene also scored a season-high 27 points in an 87–81 NIT win over [[Robert Morris University|Robert Morris]] on March 18, 2008.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280780183 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718161605/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280780183 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 18, 2012 |title=Syracuse 87, Robert Morris 81 |work=ESPN.com |date=March 18, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2013}} Greene struggled in Big East play, where he shot just 28.6 percent (40-for-140) from downtown. While he led Syracuse in scoring, he also took more shots than anyone on the team, and had more turnovers (91) than assists (71). He was also criticized for his poor shot selection and porous defense.{{cite web|last=Thamel |first=Pete |author-link=Pete Thamel |url=http://thequad.blogs.nytimes.com/2008/04/02/greenes-future-still-in-air/ |title=Greenes Future Still In Air |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 2, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2013}} Greene and [[Jonny Flynn]] were the country's second-highest scoring freshman duo.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280720222 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721070556/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280720222 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 21, 2012 |title=Orange done in by sloppy play, Villanova's 3-pointers |work=ESPN.com |date=March 12, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2013}} In April 2008, Greene declared himself eligible for the NBA draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3338322 |title=Freshman forward Greene to enter NBA draft |work=ESPN.com |date=April 9, 2008 |access-date=September 29, 2013}} ==Professional career== In the pick that they received from the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] as part of the [[Pau Gasol]] trade, the Memphis Grizzlies selected Greene with the 28th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He was later traded by Memphis to the [[Houston Rockets]]. Greene signed with the Rockets on July 15, 2008, and proceeded to score 40 points in his summer league debut at the [[Thomas & Mack Center]] in [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]]. He hit 12–20 field goals, including 5-of-10 threes, to go along with 11-of-12 [[free throw]]s.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/games/20080714/PHXHOU/recap.html |title=Greene Drops On March 11, 2013, Greene signed with the [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of Puerto Rico for the 2013 BSN season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/99802/donte-greene-moves-in-puerto-rico-with-atleticos-de-san-german.html Donte Greene moves in Puerto Rico with Atleticos de San German] On April 5, 2013, he left Atléticos after just one game. On April 17, 2013, Greene signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13069 |title=Grizzlies sign Donte Greene and Willie Reed |access-date=2013-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130512182842/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13069 |archive-date=2013-05-12 |url-status=dead }} In July 2013, he joined the Grizzlies for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On August 15, 2013, he was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Fab Melo]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-memphis|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Memphis|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 15, 2013|date=August 15, 2013}} He was waived by the Celtics on September 17, 2013.[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-waive-greene Celtics Waive Greene] Later that month, he signed with the [[Dongguan Leopards]] of China for the 2013–14 season,[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/106082/donte-greene-signing-with-dongguan.html Donte Greene signing with Dongguan] and joined the Leopards for their tour of New Zealand.[http://www.nzbreakers.co.nz/article/id/1xtgkccok0u5q1kwkfowpvdabp NBA FORWARD SIGNS WITH DONGGUAN LEOPARDS FOR NZ TOUR] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926232757/http://www.nzbreakers.co.nz/article/id/1xtgkccok0u5q1kwkfowpvdabp |date=2013-09-26 }} He scored 41 points in their first of three games against the [[New Zealand Breakers]].[http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/17wske9ix3bkl1k1lwym1d39hd Breakers take first game of Champions Challenge over Dongguan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003021356/http://www.nbl.com.au/article/id/17wske9ix3bkl1k1lwym1d39hd |date=2013-10-03 }} In July 2014, Greene joined the Brooklyn Nets for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster Brooklyn Nets Announce Summer League Roster] In December 2014, he joined Dubai's club [[Al-Nasr Dubai SC|Al-Nasr]] for the 2014–15 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/145019/donte-greene-signs-in-dubai-with-al-nasr.html Donte Greene signs in Dubai with Al-Nasr] The next season, he also played in the [[UAE National Basketball League]], but with [[Sharjah SC (basketball)|Al Sharjah]]. In May 2016, he signed with [[Ohud Medina (basketball)|Ohud Medina]] of the [[Saudi Premier League (basketball)|Saudi Premier League]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.asia-basket.com/United%20Arab%20Emirates/news/446440/Uhud-signs-Donte-Greene,-ex-Al-Sharjah-for-GCC-!!- |title=Uhud signs Donte Greene, ex Al Sharjah for GCC !! |access-date=2017-01-10 |archive-date=2017-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113040201/http://www.asia-basket.com/United%20Arab%20Emirates/news/446440/Uhud-signs-Donte-Greene,-ex-Al-Sharjah-for-GCC-!!- |url-status=dead }} In August 2016, Greene signed with the [[Leones de Santo Domingo]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Dominican%20Republic/news/459205/Donte-Greene-(ex-Uhud)-agreed-terms-with-Leones-de-Santo-Domingo |title=Donte Greene (ex Uhud) agreed terms with Leones de Santo Domingo |access-date=2017-01-10 |archive-date=2017-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113030153/http://www.latinbasket.com/Dominican%20Republic/news/459205/Donte-Greene-(ex-Uhud)-agreed-terms-with-Leones-de-Santo-Domingo |url-status=dead }} He led his team to the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto|LNB Championship]] in the Dominican Republic.
